answer.exemplar: The part's velocity keeps turning as the arm rounds the corner, so its direction changes even though its magnitude stays the same. questions.stem: A bolted steel frame carries a load that is increased very gradually while the joint stays perfectly still. Explain what the friction inside the joint is doing during that slow increase.

answer.exemplar: Static friction is self-adjusting, so as the external load creeps upward the friction force inside the joint rises to match it exactly, and the joint does not move at all. That matching continues only until the maximum static friction is reached, which is set by the coefficient of static friction multiplied by the normal force at the joint. Beyond that ceiling the joint slips suddenly, so a gradual increase in load is safe up to the limit and dangerous past it.

questions.explanation: Static friction takes whatever value is needed, up to a ceiling fixed by the coefficient and the normal force, so the joint stays still while the load grows. Past that ceiling it slips.
